title: Programming for Engineers (MATLAB)
description: Programming for Engineers (MATLAB) introduces first-year mechanical engineering students to MATLAB as a practical environment for engineering computation. The course emphasizes scripts, arrays, matrices, functions, visualization, data import, debugging, numerical methods, ODE simulation, and applied mechanical engineering mini-projects.

topics.title: MATLAB Environment, Scripts, and Engineering Workflow
topics.description: Students learn how MATLAB is organized as an engineering computing environment: command window, editor, workspace, paths, scripts, Live Scripts, and help tools.

children.title: MATLAB interface
children.description: The point is to help students become fluent in the workspace where they will write, run, inspect, and revise code.

children.title: Current folder, paths, and help documentation
Scripts and Live Scripts
children.description: Students learn when to use quick scripts, polished Live Scripts, and reusable code files.

children.title: Engineering workflow habits
children.description: This subtopic frames code as part of a repeatable engineering process, not just a calculator replacement.

topics.title: Variables, Data Types, Operators, and Expressions
topics.description: This module builds the basic language mechanics students need before they can solve engineering problems computationally.

children.title: Variables and assignment
children.description: Students learn how MATLAB stores values and how names, values, and workspace state interact.

children.title: Data types
children.description: Types affect storage, operations, and interpretation of engineering data.

children.title: Operators and expressions
children.description: This gives students the mechanics for turning formulas into executable code.

topics.title: Arrays, Vectors, Matrices, and Indexing
topics.description: Students learn MATLAB's central idea: most engineering computation becomes clearer when data is represented as arrays and matrices.

children.title: Array construction
children.description: Students learn to create the structures MATLAB is built around.

children.title: Indexing
children.description: Indexing is the gateway to extracting, replacing, and analyzing selected parts of engineering data.

children.title: Matrix operations
children.description: Students learn the difference between matrix algebra and element-by-element operations.

topics.title: Vectorization and Matrix-Based Problem Solving
topics.description: This topic helps students move from loop-by-loop thinking toward concise, efficient MATLAB expressions.

children.title: Vectorized thinking
children.description: The goal is to express whole calculations over arrays in a compact, readable form.

children.title: Performance basics
children.description: Students learn that implementation style affects speed and clarity.

children.title: Matrix problem formulation
children.description: Students practice turning engineering equations into matrix form.

topics.title: Conditionals, Loops, and Program Control
topics.description: Students learn how MATLAB programs make decisions, repeat calculations, and manage iterative engineering procedures.

children.title: Conditional logic
children.description: Students learn to choose computational paths based on data, assumptions, or engineering criteria.

children.title: Loops
children.description: Loops are necessary for iterative algorithms, simulations, and repeated operations.

children.title: Control-flow reliability
children.description: This subtopic helps students avoid common logic mistakes.

topics.title: Functions and Modular Programming
topics.description: Students learn to package calculations into reusable functions with clear inputs, outputs, and documentation.

children.title: Function files
children.description: Students learn to separate reusable calculations from one-off scripts.

children.title: Function design
children.description: Good function design makes engineering code easier to debug, test, and reuse.

children.title: Built-in and custom functions
children.description: Students learn to combine MATLAB's library tools with their own problem-specific functions.

topics.title: Plotting, Visualization, and Engineering Communication
topics.description: This module teaches students to turn numerical results into readable figures that support engineering interpretation.

children.title: Basic plots
children.description: Plots help students see trends, compare models, and communicate results.

children.title: Engineering visualization
children.description: Students learn formats common in engineering reports and labs.

children.title: Figure quality
children.description: This turns a plot from a quick check into a defensible engineering artifact.

topics.title: File Input/Output, Tables, and Data Import
topics.description: Students learn how MATLAB interacts with lab data, measurement files, spreadsheets, and structured datasets.

children.title: Reading data
children.description: Students learn how to bring experimental or design data into MATLAB.

children.title: Working with tables
children.description: Tables support named columns and mixed data, which are common in lab and test datasets.

children.title: Writing outputs
children.description: Students learn to save computational results for reports, later analysis, or collaboration.

topics.title: Debugging, Error Handling, and Code Quality
topics.description: Students practice finding mistakes, checking assumptions, and making MATLAB code easier to trust and reuse.

children.title: Debugging tools
children.description: Students learn systematic ways to locate the smallest source of a problem.

children.title: Error handling
children.description: Robust engineering scripts should fail clearly and protect against invalid inputs.

children.title: Code quality
children.description: This subtopic encourages habits that make MATLAB code easier to review and maintain.

topics.title: Numerical Methods for Engineering Problems
topics.description: This module introduces common computational methods used across engineering: root finding, interpolation, regression, integration, and linear systems.

children.title: Root finding and optimization
children.description: Students learn how computational tools solve equations that are difficult or impossible to solve by hand.

children.title: Data fitting and interpolation
children.description: Engineers often need models from data, so students practice fitting and estimating values.

children.title: Integration and linear systems
children.description: These tools appear throughout mechanics, fluids, thermal systems, and design calculations.

topics.title: ODE Solvers, Simulation, and Model-Based Computation
topics.description: Students connect programming to dynamic engineering systems by simulating models and interpreting solution behavior.

children.title: ODE modeling
children.description: Students learn to translate dynamic systems into derivative functions and initial conditions.

children.title: MATLAB ODE solvers
children.description: The goal is to use built-in solvers intelligently rather than treating them as black boxes.

children.title: Simulation interpretation
children.description: Students learn to judge whether a simulation makes engineering sense.

topics.title: Mechanical Engineering Applications and Mini-Projects
topics.description: The course closes by applying MATLAB to mechanics, design, thermal/fluid, vibrations, controls, or experimental-data problems.

children.title: Mechanics and design calculations
children.description: Students apply MATLAB to repeated calculations and parameter studies in mechanics and design.

children.title: Thermal, fluid, and vibration examples
children.description: These examples show how one computing skillset transfers across ME domains.

children.title: Integrated mini-projects
children.description: Projects bring together scripts, functions, plots, files, debugging, and explanation.

children.title: Final code, figures, and short report
